title: Perf microtraces + swimlane bands for model-route performance dashboard
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Design and spec a set of compact performance tiles and an associated swimlane/band chart for per-model and per-route performance pages. Includes microtrace detail, percentile fold views, and token-cost drilldown flows.
description:
Goal: Provide compact, composable UI primitives that show latency, throughput, and token distribution for a given model or route. These primitives will be used in the per-model overview, per-route detail, and the comparative route table.

Scope: 1) Tile set (compact summary cards) for quick health scan. 2) Swimlane / band view for concurrent throughput and latency bands over time. 3) Microtrace panel: lightweight per-request waterfall with token-level markers. 4) Cost drilldown modal that ties tokens -> compute buckets -> estimated cost per time window.

Out of scope: Full session replay, distributed tracing integration (will link to tracing page in future iteration).
decisions: Tiles are 3-up responsive: small (mobile) shows stacked single metric; medium shows 3 tiles in a row; large supports inline microtrace preview.
Default aggregation window is 1m for live view, 5m for historical ranges > 1 day. Users can override to 30s or 15m.
Latency bands will show P50/P90/P95/P99 as filled bands, with P95 outlined as the primary SLA indicator.
Swimlane uses sampling for high-cardinality routes: default 10% sampling with deterministic hashing by request id for consistent traces when toggling views.
Cost drilldown maps tokens to compute buckets using the runtime's batch size and GPU-hours heuristic; show both estimated and billed cost columns.
Microtrace view is capped to first 300 tokens and 2s of render to avoid UI jank; link out to full trace service for deeper inspection.
Charts should be implemented with the shared charting library (chartkit) and expose layer keys for telemetry tagging.
Color palette aligns with console theme: latency bands use sequential reds/oranges; throughput swimlane uses blue gradients; token markers use subtle purple.
Accessibility: all tiles must have text fallbacks for metric values and consider colorblind-friendly palette choices (protanopia-safe).
tradeoffs: High-frequency aggregation (15s) gives better insight for bursty traffic but increases backend cost; defaulted to 1m to balance cost and resolution.
Inline microtraces add immediate context but can be noisy for heavy traffic routes; limiting to sampled traces reduces noise at the cost of completeness.
Showing estimated cost in real-time is inherently approximate; we surface a confidence band and link to detailed billing for authoritative numbers.
Complexity of swimlane interactions (hover scrubbing, range select, group by model version) increases dev time; phase 1 focuses on hover scrub + click-to-modal.
Using chartkit reuses engineering effort but constrains some bespoke animations; acceptable for first delivery to maintain consistency across console.
We trade off absolute accuracy for responsiveness in the UI by pre-aggregating percentiles on the backend and applying client-side smoothing for display.
To avoid overloading the console, token-level markers are shown only when zoomed-in to a single route and time range under 1 hour.
Drilldown will provide both token-count and estimated compute; exact per-request GPU-time requires runtime instrumentation planned in a later cycle.
Prioritize read performance (cached aggregates) over fully-real-time when user selects large historical windows.
We accept that route-level swimlanes for multi-tenant Dedicated customers must respect tenant isolation; admin-only features will be gated behind RBAC in private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Design handoff assets available in Figma with component tokens and responsive states documented.
Three tile variants defined: Summary, Expanded, and Compact, with exact spacing and typography tokens.
Band chart spec: axis labels, percentiles (P50/P90/P95/P99), color mapping, tooltip payload structure, and sampling strategy documented.
Swimlane interactions: hover to highlight, click-to-open-drilldown-modal, keyboard accessible focus states.
Microtrace mock: per-request waterfall with token boundaries, approximate token timings, and link to full trace. Max render size and performance budget specified.
Cost drilldown flow mapped: entry points defined (tile chevron / swimlane context menu), modal steps, and CSV export option for tokens->cost breakdown.
Edge cases documented: low-sample routes, data gaps, incorrect timezones, and missing model version metadata.
Design review signoff from PM (Samir Chen) and eng lead (Laura Ortiz) recorded in comments.
Component checklist: accessible labels, microcopy for tooltips, loading/fallback states, and empty-state messaging included.
Design tokens exported and a minimal CSS/vars spec provided for engineering implementation.
Prototype validated in internal usability session (3 frontend engineers, 2 PMs, 1 SRE) with notes captured.
dependencies: ENG-7123: backend percentile aggregation endpoints (P50/P90/P95/P99) with sampling flags
ENG-7210: trace-service link endpoint and per-request trace fetch API
ENG-7345: billing-estimator microservice for token->cost mapping
PM-410: product decision on default retention windows and query limits
notes: 03/01: PM requested that cost estimates emphasize 'estimated' with a subtle banner and link to billing for reconciled values.
03/03: Eng flagged potential performance concern for >10k series in swimlane; agreed to enforce series cap and show aggregation message.
03/06: Usability session found users prefer percentile bands over single-line P95 graphs for quick anomaly scanning.
03/09: Accessibility pass: increased contrast on band edges and added keyboard-only reveal for microtrace preview.
03/10: Ready for final design review; addressed Laura's layout questions and uploaded final spec to Figma.
